description: IscS is the housekeeping pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP)-dependent cysteine desulfurase of Escherichia coli, a cytosolic homodimer encoded in the iscRSUA-hscBA-fdx operon. It converts L-cysteine to L-alanine and carries the released sulfane sulfur as a persulfide on its active-site Cys328, located on a flexible surface loop. From this persulfide IscS delivers sulfur to a range of acceptor proteins that bind one at a time around Cys328: the scaffold IscU for assembly of [2Fe-2S] and [4Fe-4S] clusters (with frataxin/CyaY, IscX and ferredoxin acting as modulators of the IscS-IscU complex); ThiI for 4-thiouridine formation in tRNA and for thiazole/thiamine biosynthesis; TusA, the entry point of the Tus relay that leads to MnmA-catalysed 2-thiolation of the wobble uridine; and FdhD for maturation of molybdenum formate dehydrogenases. IscS also degrades L-selenocysteine in vitro and has been implicated in selenium delivery for selenophosphate synthesis. Loss of IscS abolishes tRNA s4U and causes thiamine and nicotinic acid auxotrophy and slow growth.

description: MnmA is a cytosolic ATP-dependent tRNA-uridine 2-sulfurtransferase that incorporates sulfur at C2 of wobble uridine in tRNAs for lysine, glutamate and glutamine. It activates U34 by adenylation and couples sulfur utilization to the IscS/Tus sulfur-relay system. The physiological requirement for an iron-sulfur cofactor in this D-type MnmA and the chemistry of the terminal sulfur handoff remain unresolved.

description: TusA is a small cytosolic sulfur-carrier protein that accepts persulfide sulfur from the cysteine desulfurase IscS and supplies the TusBCD/TusE relay for C2 thiolation of tRNA wobble uridine. description: IscS1, also called YrvO, is a pyridoxal-phosphate-dependent cysteine desulfurase that mobilizes sulfur from L-cysteine for its cognate tRNA thiouridylase MnmA.
